independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived rather than accepted. Numbering: Ps 1 is an identity psalm — ps_lib.web_to_mt(1,1) returns (1,1) — so the row's dual-cite web:Ps.1.1 = oshb:Ps.1.1 is arithmetically correct (a dual-cite is not required here, but it is not wrong). The untitled claim holds at the substrate: Ps.1.0 is absent from verse_map_web.json, and psalm 1 is absent from the 116 entries of psalm_device_inventory.json superscriptions. Hebrew: the single quoted token collates at BYTE tier against oshb:Ps.1.1 (collate.py, tier=byte), and the positional claim is true — it is whitespace-token 1 of 15 in the staged extract, i.e. genuinely psalm-initial. WEB fidelity: both curly-quoted spans are verbatim; the web:Ps.1.6 quote is a clean substring that drops only the leading conjunction, not a re-cut of sense. The negative warrant was checked verse by verse rather than assumed: across web:Ps.1.1-web:Ps.1.6 there is no vocative, no imperative and no speaker change — all 6 verses of the span (unit = WEB verses) are third-person declarative — so 'no vocative address, imperative, or speaker change interrupts the movement' is verified, not asserted. Disclosure objects: pmarks_Ps.json carries zero ketiv/qere notes and zero selah verses in Ps 1, and Ps 1 is not in the acrostic inventory, so no disclosure was owed and none is fabricated. The out-of-span ref web:Ps.2.12 is properly mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs. Unit and confidence are sound: six verses, one movement, high confidence carried by a fully verified negative warrant. Observation (not a defect): device_notes describes the second leg only as 'a related word at the end of Psalm 2', which is loose but asserts no position; the row that does assert a position is where the frame fails, and I file it there rather than here.

Identity numbering re-derived: ps_lib.web_to_mt(2,1) returns (2,1); Ps.2.0 is absent from verse_map_web.json and psalm 2 is absent from the superscription inventory, so 'opens without a title' is substrate-true. All 3 curly-quoted WEB spans (unit = quoted spans) are verbatim at their refs. The seam was tested on the Hebrew, not on the translation: oshb:Ps.2.3 is first-person plural throughout — the cohortative that opens it and the second cohortative in its B-colon — while oshb:Ps.2.4 opens with a third-masculine-singular form and stays in third-person narration. That cohortative-to-narration shift is a tier-1 discourse frame visible in both witnesses, and it puts the seam exactly where the row puts it. The rejected_alternative (extending through web:Ps.2.4) is the right rival and is correctly refused. High confidence is calibrated. Observation, weighed and not filed: the first observed_substrate_signal grounds the strophe close in 'the WEB closing quotation mark'. MT oshb:Ps.2.2 has no verb of speaking introducing the quotation and MT carries no punctuation at all, so that mark is translator-supplied and is a WEB-only artifact rather than a shared-witness signal. I do not file this, because the row's second signal states the witness-independent warrant — third-person narration resuming at web:Ps.2.4 — and that signal, not the punctuation, is what carries the seam. The note is recorded so the reliance is visible.

Both quoted Hebrew runs (rationale and signal) collate at BYTE tier against oshb:Ps.2.4 (collate.py, tier=byte), and the positional claim is true: the token is whitespace-token 1 of 6, so 'the strophe opens ... beginning' is exact. Identity numbering confirmed, so web:Ps.2.4 = oshb:Ps.2.4 is correct arithmetic. WEB spans at web:Ps.2.4 and web:Ps.2.6 are verbatim. The back seam is the interesting one and it holds on the bytes: oshb:Ps.2.6 opens with a first-singular perfect in Yahweh's own voice, while oshb:Ps.2.7 opens with a first-singular cohortative in the king's voice — two different first-person speakers, not one continuous speech — so the voice distinction the row draws at web:Ps.2.6|web:Ps.2.7 is real rather than stylistic. web:Ps.2.5 is argued in prose without appearing in boundary_evidence_refs; I checked this against the settled rule before ruling, and it is not a defect — the refs-mirror obligation covers verses OUTSIDE the row's own span, and Ps.2.5 is inside it (check_refs_mirror GREEN). Two observations, neither filed: 'Yahweh's derision (web:Ps.2.4-web:Ps.2.5)' is a summary label that fits web:Ps.2.4 (laughter, derision) better than web:Ps.2.5, which is anger and terror escalating into the decree; and the signal calls the opening token 'the strophe's opening verb' where the form is a participle serving as subject. I do not file the second point because the staged OSHB extract carries no morphology layer to cite against it, and the row's own gloss renders the token substantivally, which is consistent with the form.

Both quoted Hebrew runs collate at BYTE tier against oshb:Ps.2.7 (collate.py, tier=byte); the token is whitespace-token 1 of 11, so the 'opens with' claim is exact, and 'self-referential' is right for a first-singular cohortative. All 3 curly-quoted WEB spans (unit = quoted spans) are verbatim at web:Ps.2.7, web:Ps.2.8 and web:Ps.2.9. Both seams verified independently: at the front, oshb:Ps.2.6 is Yahweh's first-singular perfect and oshb:Ps.2.7 the king's first-singular cohortative, a genuine speaker change; at the back, oshb:Ps.2.10 opens the imperative turn with two masculine-plural imperatives addressed to kings and judges, and WEB closes the decree's quotation at web:Ps.2.9. The span is bounded by text signals on both sides. Confidence 'medium' is well calibrated rather than timid: the web:Ps.2.6-web:Ps.2.9 grouping is a live rival because web:Ps.2.6 is itself divine speech, and the rejected_alternative names exactly that rival and answers it on speaker grounds. One OL-specific trap checked and cleared: oshb:Ps.2.9 is a classic cross-tradition variant site, but pmarks_Ps.json records no ketiv/qere anywhere in Ps 1-4, so no K/Q disclosure was owed here, and the row correctly makes no variant claim and cites no cross-tradition material.

The span itself is the best-warranted seam in the psalm and I do not contest it: oshb:Ps.2.10 opens with two masculine-plural imperatives addressed to kings and judges of the earth, oshb:Ps.2.11 and oshb:Ps.2.12 continue the imperative chain, and nothing in web:Ps.2.7-web:Ps.2.9 supplies an antecedent for that addressee — so the web:Ps.2.9|web:Ps.2.10 seam is byte-supported and high confidence is earned. Both quoted Hebrew tokens collate at BYTE tier against their cited refs (collate.py), the identity dual-cites are arithmetically correct, all 3 curly-quoted WEB spans (unit = quoted spans) are verbatim, and the ellipsis-joined web:Ps.2.12 quote keeps source order without re-cutting sense. The out-of-span ref web:Ps.1.1 is properly mirrored. What fails is the cross-psalm frame in device_notes, on two counts of differing weight — a false positional claim about where the second leg sits, and an inaccurate account of how the two tokens differ. The frame's substance survives both corrections; its stated evidence does not. Observation, not filed as a challenge: the phrase 'disclosed in device_notes' in the second signal is an intra-schema pointer of the kind the register rules discourage, but it contests neither span, warrant, fact nor evidence, so it fails the challenge test and I leave it as a note.

challenges.claim: device_notes calls the beatitude token at oshb:Ps.2.12 the psalm's 'closing word', but it is followed by three further tokens and does not close the verse or the psalm.
challenges.evidence: Ps 2 is an identity psalm (ps_lib.web_to_mt(2,12) = (2,12)), so web:Ps.2.12 = oshb:Ps.2.12. Spliced byte-true from verse_map_oshb.json, oshb:Ps.2.12 reads in full: “נַשְּׁקוּ בַ֡ר פֶּן יֶאֱנַ֤ף וְתֹ֬אבְדוּ דֶ֗רֶךְ כִּֽי יִבְעַ֣ר כִּמְעַ֣ט אַפּ֑וֹ אַ֝שְׁרֵ֗י כָּל ח֥וֹסֵי בֽוֹ”. The cited token “אַ֝שְׁרֵ֗י” collates at byte tier against that ref (collate.py, tier=byte), but it is whitespace-token 11 of 14 in the staged extract: three tokens follow it, “כָּל ח֥וֹסֵי בֽוֹ”, and the verse-final token is “בֽוֹ”. The finding is maqaf-independent — the staged OSHB extract is maqaf-free (maqaf serialized as space), so whether the two tokens preceding the final one are counted as one accentual unit or two, the cited token is followed by further text and closes nothing. oshb:Ps.2.12 is itself the last verse of the psalm (MT Ps 2 = 12 verses, WEB Ps 2 = 12 verses), so the error is strictly positional within the verse, not a wrong verse. The parallel leg is stated correctly, which sharpens the asymmetry: at oshb:Ps.1.1 the token “אַ֥שְֽׁרֵי” is whitespace-token 1 of 15 and is genuinely psalm-initial (byte tier). Accurate wording is available without weakening the frame: the second leg OPENS the psalm's final colon, rendered “Blessed are all those who take refuge in him” (web:Ps.2.12). Because the frame is offered as an opening-to-closing inclusio, the position is the load-bearing part of the claim, and it is the part that is false.

challenges.claim: device_notes attributes the whole difference between the two beatitude tokens to cantillation, but they also differ by a non-cantillation mark (meteg), which is why they fail accent_stripped and not only byte tier.
challenges.evidence: Both tokens spliced byte-true. oshb:Ps.1.1: “אַ֥שְֽׁרֵי” = U+05D0 U+05B7 U+05A5 U+05E9 U+05C1 U+05B0 U+05BD U+05E8 U+05B5 U+05D9. oshb:Ps.2.12: “אַ֝שְׁרֵ֗י” = U+05D0 U+05B7 U+059D U+05E9 U+05C1 U+05B0 U+05E8 U+05B5 U+0597 U+05D9. Cantillation does differ (U+05A5 against U+059D plus U+0597), but meteg U+05BD is present in the oshb:Ps.1.1 token and absent from the oshb:Ps.2.12 token, and meteg is not cantillation. By the toolkit's own tier definition — accent_stripped strips U+0591-U+05AF only and RETAINS U+05BD — the pair therefore fails accent_stripped as well: the accent_stripped forms are U+05D0 U+05B7 U+05E9 U+05C1 U+05B0 U+05BD U+05E8 U+05B5 U+05D9 against U+05D0 U+05B7 U+05E9 U+05C1 U+05B0 U+05E8 U+05B5 U+05D9. Measured rather than argued: collating the oshb:Ps.2.12 token against the oshb:Ps.1.1 verse window returns tier=skeleton — the pair matches at 1 of the 4 tiers collate.py ranks (byte no, nfd no, accent_stripped no, skeleton yes). The row's tier label is therefore correct; the defect is the stated reason, not the tier. Context for why the reason matters: a skeleton sweep of the consonantal string returns 31 MT verses (sweep.py --skel, unit = verses), and that figure is a contiguous-substring count that conflates the beatitude construct with unrelated 'step' forms at oshb:Ps.17.5 and oshb:Ps.17.11, so skeleton identity by itself is a weak relation and the frame's force rests on position.

reviews.reasoning: Every number in this row was re-derived through ps_lib rather than trusted. Ps 3 is shift+1: web_to_mt(3,1) = (3,2), and verse_map_web.json records Ps.3.0 with mt_title_verses ['Ps.3.1'], so web:Ps.3.0 = oshb:Ps.3.1 is the correct title pseudo-ref form. The three selah dual-cites are each exact — mt_to_web maps oshb:Ps.3.3 to web:Ps.3.2, oshb:Ps.3.5 to web:Ps.3.4, and oshb:Ps.3.9 to web:Ps.3.8. The selah disclosure is complete and span-scoped, not spot-checked: pmarks_Ps.json lists exactly 3 selah verses in Ps 3 (unit = MT verses) and the row discloses all 3, so the symmetry requirement is satisfied by sweep rather than by sample. I also verified the 'closes' wording against the bytes — in all 3 verses the selah token is verse-final. Most importantly the row handles selah correctly as evidence: it is called corroboration of internal pauses, and the rejected_alternative refuses a three-part split precisely because the pause is not an independent seam driver. That is the right ruling under the evidence rules, and it is the reason medium confidence is properly calibrated for a whole-psalm unit that had a visible rival. Title labels match the inventory exactly: psalm_device_inventory.json superscriptions['3'] carries labels mizmor and le_david, which is what device_notes claims, no more. The WEB title quote is verbatim. The negative addressee claim was checked verse by verse rather than accepted: across all 8 WEB verses of the span (unit = verses) there are exactly 2 vocative sites, both to Yahweh — web:Ps.3.1 and web:Ps.3.7 (the latter carrying 'my God' in the same verse), so 'without a vocative shift to a different addressee' is verified. No K/Q notes exist in Ps 3, none are claimed; no pe/samekh claim appears, correctly, since that layer is absent from WLC Psalms entirely. MT Ps 3 = 9 verses against WEB 8, consistent with the title counted as MT v1. The cross_part_phrasing_variation flag is logged bookkeeping and I treat it as such.

I do not assert that the span is wrong — an 8-verse psalm carried as one row is policy-compliant, and I reached no rival seam I would defend as better. What I contest is the evidence offered for it, which does not survive re-derivation. The citation arithmetic is exact throughout — Ps 4 is shift+1, and web:Ps.4.0 = oshb:Ps.4.1, web:Ps.4.2 = oshb:Ps.4.3, web:Ps.4.4 = oshb:Ps.4.5 all check through ps_lib, with mt_title_verses ['Ps.4.1'] confirming the title pseudo-ref. Selah handling is exemplary and I verified it as a sweep, not a sample: pmarks_Ps.json lists exactly 2 selah verses in Ps 4 (unit = MT verses), oshb:Ps.4.3 and oshb:Ps.4.5, both verse-final, and both are disclosed; the front-seam occurrence at oshb:Ps.3.9 = web:Ps.3.8 is disclosed AND correctly attributed to the preceding psalm rather than annexed as evidence for this one. Title labels are consistent with psalm_device_inventory.json superscriptions['4'] (mizmor, lamnatseach, le_david, binginot): the rationale names three and the signals name three, each a true subset, neither framed as exhaustive, so I do not treat the partial lists as a defect. No K/Q notes exist in Ps 4 and none are claimed. What fails is the addressee map — the very evidence the whole-psalm warrant rests on. I swept it across all 8 WEB verses (unit = verses), checking the MT morphology of each: second-person address to Yahweh occupies 4 verses in 2 runs (web:Ps.4.1; web:Ps.4.6-web:Ps.4.8) and address to the human audience occupies 4 verses in 1 unbroken run (web:Ps.4.2-web:Ps.4.5). That is a psalm falling into 3 contiguous addressee blocks, not the fine-grained alternation the row describes. Two distinct claims fail against that map, and I file them separately because they sit in different fields and would need different repairs: the rationale misassigns web:Ps.4.5 and contradicts the row's own signals, and the rejected_alternative refuses the strophe rival on a ground the text does not support. The consequence is not that the span is wrong but that the rival is left unanswered on the merits, and 'high' confidence is not calibrated to a warrant that contradicts itself about which verse addresses whom.

challenges.claim: The rationale assigns web:Ps.4.5 to a block of direct address to Yahweh running to the psalm's close, but that verse addresses the human audience with Yahweh in the third person, and the row's own observed_substrate_signals assigns the same verse to the opposite block.
challenges.evidence: Ps 4 is shift+1, so web:Ps.4.5 = oshb:Ps.4.6 and web:Ps.4.6 = oshb:Ps.4.7 (ps_lib.web_to_mt). web:Ps.4.5 reads in full “Offer the sacrifices of righteousness. Put your trust in Yahweh.” (web:Ps.4.5) — two second-person imperatives aimed at the human audience, with Yahweh named in the third person as the object of trust, not addressed. The MT settles it byte-true: oshb:Ps.4.6 reads “זִבְח֥וּ זִבְחֵי צֶ֑דֶק וּ֝בִטְח֗וּ אֶל יְהוָֽה”, whose two masculine-plural imperatives govern the divine name as the object of a preposition. Swept across all 8 WEB verses of the psalm (unit = verses), with the MT of each verse checked for person and vocative, second-person address to Yahweh occurs in 4 verses — web:Ps.4.1 = oshb:Ps.4.2, web:Ps.4.6 = oshb:Ps.4.7, web:Ps.4.7 = oshb:Ps.4.8 (masculine-singular perfect), web:Ps.4.8 = oshb:Ps.4.9 (masculine-singular independent pronoun with the divine name as vocative) — and web:Ps.4.5 is not one of them. Address to Yahweh resumes at the next verse: oshb:Ps.4.7 reads “רַבִּ֥ים אֹמְרִים֮ מִֽי יַרְאֵ֪נ֫וּ ט֥וֹב נְֽסָה עָ֭לֵינוּ א֨וֹר פָּנֶ֬יךָ יְהוָֽה”, carrying a masculine-singular imperative, a second-person singular suffix and the divine name as vocative, rendered “Yahweh, let the light of your face shine on us” (web:Ps.4.6). So the Yahweh-address block is web:Ps.4.6-web:Ps.4.8, not web:Ps.4.5-web:Ps.4.8. The row states the correct version elsewhere: its observed_substrate_signals place the 'sons of men' addressee at web:Ps.4.2 and web:Ps.4.4-web:Ps.4.5 and Yahweh at web:Ps.4.1 and web:Ps.4.6-web:Ps.4.8 — directly contradicting the rationale on web:Ps.4.5. The same enumeration also leaves web:Ps.4.3 = oshb:Ps.4.4 unassigned, though its masculine-plural imperative places it with the human-audience block. Severity is medium, not high, because the alternation warrant and therefore the span survive the correction — the corrected map still alternates rather than blocking — but the misassigned verse sits inside the row's load-bearing evidence, and the row carries high confidence while contradicting itself about it.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative refuses a strophe split on the ground that both addressees recur more than once instead of occupying separate blocks, but the verified addressee map is exactly blocks — the human audience is addressed in 1 unbroken run of 4 verses — so the rival is refused on a ground the text does not support.
challenges.evidence: Swept across all 8 WEB verses of Ps 4 (unit = verses), each verse checked against its MT counterpart under the shift+1 mapping. Address to the human audience runs unbroken over 4 verses, web:Ps.4.2-web:Ps.4.5, and every one of them carries masculine-plural forms: oshb:Ps.4.3 (vocative 'sons of man' with two 2mp verbs), oshb:Ps.4.4 “וּדְע֗וּ כִּֽי הִפְלָ֣ה יְ֭הוָה חָסִ֣יד ל֑וֹ יְהוָ֥ה יִ֝שְׁמַ֗ע בְּקָרְאִ֥י אֵלָֽיו” (2mp imperative, with the divine name in the third person twice), oshb:Ps.4.5 “רִגְז֗וּ וְֽאַל תֶּ֫חֱטָ֥אוּ אִמְר֣וּ בִ֭לְבַבְכֶם עַֽל מִשְׁכַּבְכֶ֗ם וְדֹ֣מּוּ סֶֽלָה” (four 2mp forms including two 2mp suffixes), and oshb:Ps.4.6 “זִבְח֥וּ זִבְחֵי צֶ֑דֶק וּ֝בִטְח֗וּ אֶל יְהוָֽה”. Address to Yahweh occupies the remaining 4 verses in 2 runs, web:Ps.4.1 and web:Ps.4.6-web:Ps.4.8. The resulting verse-level map is 1 + 4 + 3 — three contiguous blocks with no verse-level interleaving. Both halves of the stated ground therefore fail: the human addressee does not 'recur more than once' (it occurs in exactly 1 run), and the addressees do 'occupy separate blocks'. This matters beyond wording because it is the row's only stated reason for refusing a strophe split, and the split it refuses would fall at the two block edges. I do not conclude that the split is right: a real counter-argument exists that the row does not make — the final block's first verse, web:Ps.4.6 = oshb:Ps.4.7, opens with a third-party report before turning to the vocative, so the transition is mixed in texture even though it is clean at verse granularity, and oshb:Ps.4.4 addresses the human audience while speaking about Yahweh in the third person. Severity is medium rather than high because the rival is left unanswered rather than shown to win, and the whole-psalm unit may well be correct on a warrant the row has not yet stated.
